$comment: Reviewed identities for Evangelizo Syriac English (SYE) and Arabic (SYA), 2026-01-01 through 2026-06-30. Exact source names are matched by name and biography, never by date or array position. English canonical metadata is either existing source/catalog wording or a faithful descriptive rendering of the Arabic name. Source class suffixes remain in Arabic captions.
reviewNotes: 2026-01-12: SYA biography identifies Barses/Barsa, bishop of Edessa 361-378; SYE names Bartimaeus of Edessa. Kept distinct because the names disagree and SYE supplies no biography.
2026-02-14: SYA biography explicitly identifies Pope Sixtus III (432-440). SYE Custos is not merged without evidence that its ambiguous name denotes this pope.

2026-03-09: SYA title says forty-two, but its biography explicitly describes forty soldiers of Sebaste and the frozen lake. Identity matches SYE Forty Martyrs of Sebaste; original Arabic title is retained unchanged.
2026-03-31: SYA names Abda of Seleucia and Benjamin the Deacon, with a Benjamin biography. SYE Servant of the high priest of Seleucia and companions is ambiguous and remains separate.
2026-04-13: SYA biography identifies Serapion of Thmuis, bishop and confessor; SYE identifies Serapion of Alexandria as a martyr. Kept distinct.
2026-05-13: SYA biography identifies seventh-century Isaac of Nineveh. SYE names Isaac the Teacher and Claukaria, martyrs; kept distinct.
2026-05-31: SYA biography identifies the Cappadocian soldier Hermias, martyred in 160. SYE Hermes lacks identifying details; kept distinct.

The plain SYE name St. John is reused for John the Hermit (January 15, UUID 84b37031-a409-b4e0-0266-6d090df31237) and John the Evangelist (May 8, UUID 48fb9af2-a730-ad89-54fd-0509dec8475a). englishSaintIds uses the source UUID and its explicit description to distinguish these identities; no global St. John alias is defined.
